claim: TNFα signaling in the vascular endothelium elicits multiple inflammatory responses that drive vascular destabilization and leakage.
source: TNFα signaling in the vascular endothelium elicits multiple inflammatory responses that drive vascular destabilization and leakage.
evidence: This is a general statement about TNFα effects, drawing from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Bioactive lipids are main drivers of vascular destabilization and leakage processes.
source: Bioactive lipids are main drivers of these processes.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about the role of bioactive lipids in vascular processes.

claim: Two-dimensional endothelial cell cultures often display a pro-inflammatory phenotype due to lack of laminar flow and growth on non-compliant stiff substrates.
source: In vitro mechanistic studies of bioactive lipids have been largely based on two-dimensional endothelial cell cultures that, due to lack of laminar flow and the growth of the cells on non-compliant stiff substrates, often display a pro-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the manuscript and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The pro-inflammatory phenotype of 2D cultures complicates the assessment of inflammatory processes.
source: This complicates the assessment of inflammatory processes.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the previous statement about 2D culture limitations.

claim: Three-dimensional microvessels-on-a-chip models provide a unique opportunity to generate endothelial microvessels in a more physiological environment.
source: Three-dimensional microvessels-on-a-chip models provide a unique opportunity to generate endothelial microvessels in a more physiological environment.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental design and citations to prior work on the platform.

claim: Bioactive lipid profiles can be readily detected from three-dimensional microvessels-on-a-chip.
source: We demonstrate that bioactive lipid profiles can be readily detected from three-dimensional microvessels-on-a-chip and display a more dynamic, less inflammatory response to TNFα, that resembles more the human situation, compared to classical two-dimensional endothelial cell cultures.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript showing detection of multiple bioactive lipids.

claim: 3D microvessels display a more dynamic, less inflammatory response to TNFα compared to 2D endothelial cell cultures.
source: We demonstrate that bioactive lipid profiles can be readily detected from three-dimensional microvessels-on-a-chip and display a more dynamic, less inflammatory response to TNFα, that resembles more the human situation, compared to classical two-dimensional endothelial cell cultures.

claim: The response of 3D microvessels to TNFα resembles more the human situation than 2D cultures.

claim: TNFα is a central mediator of the inflammatory response.

claim: TNFα signaling in endothelial cells involves the activation of NFκB.
source: Mechanistically, TNFα signaling in endothelial cells involves the activation of NFκB and results in the increased synthesis of reactive oxygen species (ROS) from a number of sources such as mitochondria, NADPH oxidase, uncoupled eNOS, xanthine oxidase, and peroxidases (Cai and Harrison, 2000; Blaser et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cai and Harrison, 2000; Blaser et al., 2016.

claim: Under physiologic conditions, bioactive lipids are critically involved in the first response of endothelial cells to environmental changes.

claim: TNFα has been identified as an important therapeutic target to counteract vascular inflammation.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Sedger and McDermott, 2014; Esposito and Cuzzocrea, 2009.
